public_rationale: Firsthand launch reviews repeatedly encountered failures in advertised food-ordering and ride-booking functions. That supports the ordinary qualitative reading of barely functioning. A successful sandwich order shows that some actions worked, but does not overturn the evidence of serious unreliability. The finding concerns the launch experience, not later versions.
limitations: The phrase has no numerical threshold.
Reviewers tested limited accounts, locations and tasks.
Evidence dates identify reported performance snapshots; individual test days are not consistently supplied.
These tests establish user-visible performance, not which internal component caused each failure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Setting aside its security concerns, Rabbit's Large Action Model looks like it barely functions.

statement.excerpt: Putting aside the remarkable security concerns, the “Large Action Model” also looks like barely-functioning dogshit.

our_interpretation: The ordinary factual reading is that the advertised app-action features were highly unreliable in practical launch-period use, with repeated failures or substantial delays.
This does not mean that every action failed or that every R1 feature was unusable.
Use the April 23 launch through the May 13 post, reflecting the launch demo and recent reviews discussed in context.
No numerical success-rate threshold is supplied, so assess the qualitative claim against firsthand task reports.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous firsthand tests repeatedly fail to complete core advertised app actions, or show delays and errors that make them unreliable for ordinary use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporaneous tests show core advertised app actions completing reliably with practical response times; isolated bugs would not establish barely functioning.
